sources.entry: cloudpickle - Extends pickle to functions, lambdas, and interactively defined classes, for shipping code to remote workers.

summary.one_liner: cloudpickle extends Python's pickle so that lambdas, interactively defined functions and classes, and other constructs the standard module cannot handle can be serialized and shipped to remote workers.
summary.what_it_does: Serializes Python objects that the standard pickle module rejects, including lambda functions and functions or classes defined interactively in __main__ (scripts, shells, Jupyter notebooks). It pickles these by value, while standard pickle pickles functions and classes by reference to their module. It provides register_pickle_by_value and unregister_pickle_by_value so that modules importable on the client but not on workers can be serialized by value (marked experimental). The README says it is intended for cluster computing, where code is sent over the network to remote hosts. Loading is done with the normal pickle.loads.
use_cases: ship lambda functions to remote workers
send interactively defined functions to a cluster
pickle functions defined in a Jupyter notebook
send code to workers that lack the source module
notable: Pickles lambdas and __main__-defined functions and classes by value, which standard pickle cannot do
register_pickle_by_value API (since 2.0.0) to force by-value serialization for a module, experimental
Used in PySpark, originally developed by picloud.com
Client and worker must run the exact same Python version
caveats: Only works between the exact same Python version on both ends
Not supported or recommended for long-term object storage
Unpickling untrusted data can execute arbitrary code; only load pickle data from trusted sources
register_pickle_by_value is experimental and can fail if by-value functions contain import statements or mix with by-reference functions
